title: Pawns on both wings: count, then stop or ignore
outcomes: Counts the moves of the free pawn and the king's steps to the enemy advance before choosing between stopping it and ignoring it
Predicts that moving one king by one step can change a win into a draw, and checks the prediction
Finds the winning first move in a position where stopping wins and the push does not

steps.text: In **Pawns on both wings: push, stop or march the king** you chose a first move. Now count it. For each plan, count your own moves and the enemy king's steps to the pawns he must stop. Stopping a counter-advance costs time; ignoring it can cost a pawn or the race. *Rule of thumb*: stop when your king reaches the advance in time and the push would be slower; push when the push is faster. One king step can flip the verdict.

steps.text: **The verdict flips.** In the next positions the same pawns and one king step give opposite results: a king one file nearer or further changes the count. Do not copy a pattern from one position. Predict win or draw first, then check; the tablebase result is the test, and the counts are a *rule of thumb* for predicting it.
